# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-ref

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

`coop --git` (two agents with messaging and a shared git remote) with the frozen reference settings (`gemini-3.8-flash` on Vertex AI, `medium` thinking, 500 steps, compaction at 128K tokens, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap) on `core`, 10 harder pairs, 3 of which have both features changing the same function. Comparing it pair by pair with [`solo` on the same pairs](../solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-core-ref/summary.md) (6/10) shows whether two agents lose pairs on `core` that one agent solves, now that budget no longer cuts anyone off.

## Observations

- 5/10 (50%) vs. 6/10 for `solo` with the same settings. Pair by pair, the only difference is `llama_index_task/17244` (5,6), where `solo` passed and `coop --git` passed only feature A; no pair passed only here.
- All 10 pairs merged cleanly (9 clean, 1 identical), including the 3 same-function pairs. In the earlier 100-step run, 2 of those 3 hit merge conflicts. Agents exchanged 18 to 43 messages per pair.
- On the 3 same-function pairs, `coop --git` got exactly the same partial results as `solo` (`dspy_task/8563` and `go_chi_task/27` feature B only, `react_hook_form_task/153` feature A only). These failures come from the features themselves being hard, not from coordination.
- Cost `$21.62` (`$2.16` per pair), 110 minutes at 4 pairs at a time, 33 retries, and no false notices that a partner had stopped.
